title: Double-pot two plants in a planter on risers, each pot rim 10-20 mm below its rim
instruction: Double-pot the two potted plants in the grey trough planter. For each plant, stand one of its white risers on a grey disc on the planter floor, then set the plant's pot on top of that riser so the pot's rim ends 10 to 20 mm below the planter's rim. The risers differ in height: choose the one that gives that gap. Leave both pots standing upright, one on each disc, then let go and move both grippers away from the pots.
context: Interior plantscape technicians and garden-centre display staff double-pot plants: the grow pot is set into a decorative planter on a riser (a foam puck or upturned pot) chosen so the grow pot's rim sits a little below the planter's, where top-dressing hides it, with its base clear of drainage water. Too high, the grow pot shows; too low, the plant looks sunk and is hard to water. The check is a straightedge across the planter rim and a ruler down to each pot's rim; with 7 cm pots the usual few cm is scaled to 10-20 mm. Unlike Stand sample tubes in a water bath with every top above the water line, where each tube goes on a fixed rack or the floor, here the robot first builds each support from three loose risers laid out in a different order on each side, judging pot and riser heights together; once the pot is on, the riser is hidden. Done by: landscaping and groundskeeping workers (O*NET 37-3011.00) who maintain interior plantings.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Positions are in cm. (1) Planter: a charcoal-grey (sRGB 0.20, 0.21, 0.22) glazed fibreglass trough (a painted wooden box serves for real trials), fixed to the table, open on top: 17.6 cm along x, 35.6 cm along y and 8.6 cm tall outside, walls 8 mm thick, floor 5 mm thick, centred at x 27.0, y 0, sides parallel to x and y. Inside it is 16.0 cm (x 19.0 to 35.0) by 34.0 cm (y -17.0 to +17.0); its rim (the walls' top) is 8.6 cm above the table and its floor's top 0.5 cm. (2) Two discs: light-grey (sRGB 0.55, 0.55, 0.55) vinyl discs, 9.0 cm across and 1 mm thick, fixed on the planter floor, centred at x 27.0, y +11.0 and at x 27.0, y -11.0 (the two places for the plants); their tops are 0.6 cm above the table. (3) Pot A: a bulb pan, a terracotta-coloured (sRGB 0.74, 0.40, 0.25) plastic grow pot filled with potting mix, a closed straight-sided cylinder 7.0 cm across and 3.5 cm tall, 100 g, loose, standing upright on the table centred at x 20.0, y +38.5. (4) Pot B: an azalea pot, the same but 4.6 cm tall and 130 g, standing upright at x 20.0, y -38.5. The plants are left out (a filled pot, or a turned wooden cylinder of the same size and mass, reproduces one). (5) Six risers: white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.95) high-density rigid foam pucks, solid cylinders 6.0 cm across, loose, standing upright on the table: 2.0 cm tall (15 g), 3.0 cm (22 g) and 4.2 cm (30 g). Left set, all at y +26.0: 2.0 cm at x 17.0, 3.0 cm at x 27.0, 4.2 cm at x 37.0. Right set, all at y -26.0: 3.0 cm at x 17.0, 4.2 cm at x 27.0, 2.0 cm at x 37.0. Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot; tape outlines on the table mark each loose part's start. With a straight-down grip only the left arm reaches pot A and the left set, and only the right arm reaches pot B and the right set; both arms reach the planter.
scoring: Read every control step (20 Hz). Pots and risers are the same either end up. A pot's 'rim gap' is how far the highest point of its top rim is below the planter's rim (8.6 cm above the table), in mm (negative above it): the height of its top face's centre plus 35 mm x sin(tilt). A pot is 'set' when all of these hold: (a) it stands upright, its axis within 3 degrees of vertical; (b) its centre, seen from above, is within 20 mm of a disc's centre (its outline at most 10 mm past the 9 cm disc); (c) it rests on a riser: the centre of its bottom face is within 1.5 mm (up or down) of the centre of that riser's top face, and the two are within 35 mm of each other seen from above (two risers of one height side by side under it count as one); (d) that riser stands upright (within 2 degrees) with the centre of its bottom face 4 to 7.5 mm above the table: on the planter floor (5 mm) or a disc (6 mm), not on another riser, a pot or the table; (e) it is still: its centre moved along a path shorter than 3 mm over the last 0.5 s; (f) it is let go and the grippers moved away: each gripper's tool point (between its finger pads) is at least 60 mm from the pot's centre (no grip holds a pot from that far; an open gripper left hovering closer does not count). A set pot is 'staged' when its rim gap is 10 to 20 mm. Score 1.0 if both pots are staged; 0.5 if exactly one is; 0.25 if neither is staged but at least one is set (on the wrong riser, so its rim is too high or too low); 0 in every other case: nothing done, a pot on the floor or a disc with no riser, on two stacked risers, on a riser lying on its side, tilted more than 2 degrees or standing on the table, tipped, still held or a gripper not moved away, still moving, off its disc, outside the planter or left on the table. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Every limit is inclusive except 'shorter than'. The trial ends with success once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise the score is read at the last step at the run limit with the same rules. There is no whole-trial rule: a part pushed or dropped into place is scored as it ends. For reference, with the riser on a disc: pot A's rim gap is 25, 15 and 3 mm on the 2.0, 3.0 and 4.2 cm risers (45 mm with no riser); pot B's is 14, 4 and -8 mm (34 mm with no riser); a riser on the bare floor adds 1 mm; no stack of two risers gives 10 to 20 mm. So only pot A on a 3.0 cm riser and pot B on a 2.0 cm riser are staged; however the limits above stack, no other riser reaches 10 to 20 mm (pot A on the 2.0 cm riser stays 20.2 mm or more down). One arm alone, reaching only its own side, can score 0.5. Real trial, before touching anything: check that each pot is upright and still, measure each pot's centre to its disc's centre on the photo from above, lay a straightedge across the planter's rim and measure down to the highest point of each pot's rim with a ruler (the rim gap); then lift each pot out and check that it sat on one upright riser standing on the floor or a disc.
fidelity: Rigid stand-ins: the pots are solid straight-sided cylinders with the mass of a filled grow pot (the plant and loose soil are left out; real grow pots taper), the risers rigid foam pucks, the planter a fixed open box and the discs thin fixed plates. One friction for all contacts (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The rim gap is computed from the pot's pose; a real trial reads it with a straightedge and ruler. The scorer reads the grippers' tool points to check that both let go and moved away.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the pots and risers out of the planter and stand each upright on its tape outline: pot A at x 20.0, y +38.5 and pot B at x 20.0, y -38.5 (cm); the left risers (2.0, 3.0 and 4.2 cm tall) at x 17, 27 and 37, y +26.0; the right risers (3.0, 4.2 and 2.0 cm tall) at x 17, 27 and 37, y -26.0. The planter and its discs stay fixed.
